anchor: Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme: maturity-linked redemption and gold-price-based repayment
argumentsAgainst: The source record does not establish whether the notified redemption price is financially attractive relative to an individual investor’s purchase price, because the issue price and holding-specific returns are not provided.
Gold-price-linked repayment exposes the investor’s rupee return to movements in gold prices; this is an analytical implication, not a fact stated in the press release.
argumentsFor: The mechanism links final repayment to an objectively published benchmark: the simple average of closing prices for 999-purity gold over the previous three business days.

An eight-year maturity can support longer-term investment in a sovereign-backed gold-linked instrument, while reducing the need for physical gold holdings; the latter is contextual analysis rather than a fact in this release.
background: The RBI press release concerns the final redemption of SGB 2018-19 Series-II, whose issue date was October 23, 2018. It states that repayment occurs on expiry of eight years from issue.

The redemption price is calculated in Indian rupees using the simple average of closing prices of 999-purity gold for the previous three business days, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA).
indiaImplications: The case illustrates how a government-linked financial instrument can mobilise household savings through a transparent, market-referenced redemption formula.

For public finance and monetary policy, gold-linked instruments can be discussed in relation to financialisation of savings and reduced dependence on physical gold imports, but those broader outcomes are not measured in the supplied record.

cloze.prompt: The final redemption date of the above tranche shall be ____.

officialFacts.text: In terms of GOI notification F.No.4(22)-B(W&M)/2018 dated October 08, 2018 (SGB 2018-19 Series-II-Issue date October 23, 2018) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, the Gold Bond shall be repayable on the expiration of eight years from the date of issue of the Gold Bonds. Accordingly, the final redemption date of the above tranche shall be October 23, 2026.

Accordingly, the redemption price for final redemption due on October 23, 2026, shall be ₹14,425/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand Four Hundred and Twenty-Five only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., October 19, October 21, and October 22, 2026.

The redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA).

staticDefinition: A Sovereign Gold Bond is a government-linked financial instrument whose redemption value, for the tranche covered here, is determined at final maturity through the prescribed gold-price benchmark rather than physical delivery of gold; the supplied record specifically establishes the eight-year repayment rule and benchm
use: Use this case to illustrate rule-based valuation, benchmark transparency, financialisation of savings, and the distinction between final maturity and premature redemption in GS3 economy answers.

advisory_notes: “Financialisation of savings” and reduced physical-gold imports are analytical implications, not findings established by this release.
“Sovereign-backed” and “dematerialised” are broadly relevant descriptions, but the supplied release does not itself establish every instrument feature or delivery mode.
The note should distinguish the release’s three-business-day formula from the broader scheme rule that permits premature redemption after the fifth year on interest-payment dates.[1][3]
The headline, deck and pocketRead accurately identify the tranche, maturity date and notified price as supported by the supplied RBI extract [P1].
The hypothetical example is appropriately labelled and does not assert a real future event.
The applied-question answer is analytically sound, but “investor predictability” should not imply predictable returns; the formula provides procedural transparency, while gold prices remain variable.
GS3.1 and GS3.2 are internal taxonomy codes rather than official UPSC labels; the substantive GS3 economy connection is defensible through resource mobilisation and financial-sector themes.
The ₹14,425 figure is a notified redemption price, not by itself a measure of total return; the note correctly flags the missing entry-price and holding-specific information.

wayForward: Publish redemption dates and benchmark methodology prominently through issuing and servicing channels.
Explain clearly that a notified final redemption price is not, by itself, an investor’s total return; entry price and other applicable terms also matter.
Maintain consistent disclosure of the purity standard, reference institution, averaging window and applicable redemption date.
Strengthen investor education so holders distinguish final redemption from any separate premature-redemption route.
